Compare groups of cores on single indices

Source: R/group_tests.R
compare_indices.Rd

Compares groups of cores on one index at a time, such as the rarefied SPI, ER and IR of spi_ei_batch() or the CPI and PRA summaries of cpi_pra_batch(). Each index is tested for a difference in group means with Welch-type tests, which allow the groups to have unequal variances, and every pair of groups gets a standardised mean difference with a bootstrap confidence interval.

Usage

compare_indices(
  data,
  cols,
  group,
  alpha = 0.05,
  p_adjust = "holm",
  boot = 9999,
  seed = 2226
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per core.

cols

Names of the index columns to compare.

group

The groups: the name of a column of data, or a vector with one value per row. The order of the factor levels (or of the sorted values) sets which group is group1 in each pair.

alpha

Significance level used in the notes. Default 0.05.

p_adjust

Method for adjusting the pairwise p values within each index, passed to stats::p.adjust(). Default "holm".

boot

Number of bootstrap resamples for the confidence interval of the standardised mean difference; 0 for none. Default 9999.

seed

Seed set before the bootstrap of each pair; the caller's random stream is restored afterwards. NULL uses the current stream. Default 2226.

Value

An object of class spharmlithic_index_comparison, a list with

overall

A tibble with one row per index: index, test ("Welch t" for two groups, "Welch ANOVA" for more), statistic, df1, df2 (NA for the t test), p, n_groups and n.

pairwise

A tibble with one row per index and pair of groups: index, group1, group2, n1, n2, mean1, mean2, smd (standardised mean difference, group1 minus group2), smd_lower, smd_upper (95% bootstrap interval), p (Welch t test) and p_adj.

settings

The arguments used.

Details

Two groups are compared with Welch's t test, three or more with Welch's one-way ANOVA (stats::oneway.test()) followed by Welch t tests between every pair, adjusted by p_adjust within each index (not across indices, each index answering its own question). Welch-type tests are used because differences in scar count can leave groups with unequal variances.

The standardised mean difference is the difference between the group means divided by the square root of the mean of the two group variances; its absolute value is the effect size reported by Xiao et al. (in prep.). The 95% interval is a percentile bootstrap stratified by group: each group is resampled with replacement within itself.

Which columns. Raw SPI, ER and IR shift with the scar count; compare groups with the rarefied values (*_rarefied). A message is given when a *_raw column is passed. The mean and GMD of CPI and PRA do not need rarefying.

Missing values are left out index by index, and so are groups with fewer than two cores.

References

Welch, B. L. (1951). On the comparison of several mean values: an alternative approach. Biometrika, 38(3/4), 330–336.

Holm, S. (1979). A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 6(2), 65–70.

See also

spi_ei_batch(), cpi_pra_batch(), compare_groups()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(Typology = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), each = 10),
                SPI_rarefied = rnorm(30, rep(c(0.5, 0.6, 0.6), each = 10), 0.08),
                IR_rarefied = rnorm(30, 0.2, 0.05))
compare_indices(d, c("SPI_rarefied", "IR_rarefied"), "Typology", boot = 999)
#> Index comparison (Welch tests; pairwise p adjusted by holm within each index)
#> 
#>         index        test statistic df1   df2        p n_groups  n
#>  SPI_rarefied Welch ANOVA  6.086079   2 17.68 0.009747        3 30
#>   IR_rarefied Welch ANOVA  0.001611   2 17.18 0.998391        3 30
#> 
#> Pairwise: standardised mean difference (group1 - group2) with 95% bootstrap interval (999 resamples) 
#>         index group1 group2 n1 n2      smd smd_lower smd_upper        p   p_adj
#>  SPI_rarefied      A      B 10 10 -1.45968   -3.4402   -0.4970 0.004728 0.01418
#>  SPI_rarefied      A      C 10 10 -1.12794   -2.8638   -0.2478 0.021727 0.04345
#>  SPI_rarefied      B      C 10 10  0.37718   -0.4435    1.4689 0.410214 0.41021
#>   IR_rarefied      A      B 10 10 -0.01888   -0.9173    0.8941 0.966835 1.00000
#>   IR_rarefied      A      C 10 10 -0.02478   -0.9204    1.0702 0.956461 1.00000
#>   IR_rarefied      B      C 10 10 -0.01120   -0.8950    1.1002 0.980354 1.00000
